text: The treasurer of the Winners Athletic Club has provided the following information for the year
Receipts from shop sales 6 670 Purchases for shop 2 590
Sales of tickets for events 3 720 Wages for shop 2 780
Sales of old equipment 1 200 Costs of events 2 120
1 The treasurer has found out that $60 of the trade receivables will not be received.
Bank charges of $126 have not been entered in the books.
The subscriptions include seven life memberships of $300 each. The life membership fund is
to be transferred to income and expenditure over a 10-year period.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Prepare an income statement for the shop for the year ended 30 June 2015.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Prepare the income and expenditure account for the year ended 30 June 2015.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: Prepare the statement of financial position at 30 June 2015.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text:
Explain why no amounts have been entered in the financial statements in respect of the
many hours worked during the year by volunteers.

parts.label: (e)
parts.text:
Explain why the amounts prepaid and accrued are included in the financial statements of the
club.

3 A division of Hobbs Limited manufactures one product, the Wye. The directors had prepared the
following forecast for the year ending 30 June 2016.
$000
Sales revenue 4400
Direct materials 1400
Direct labour 1000
Variable administration costs 400
Fixed administration costs 300
Other fixed overheads 1200
Budgeted sales for the year ending 30 June 2016 are expected to be 40 000 units.
REQUIRED

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Calculate for product Wye:

parts.label: (i)
parts.text: the contribution per unit

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text: the budgeted break-even point in units

parts.label: (iii)
parts.text:
the margin of safety in units

Additional information
The directors have been warned that trading conditions are likely to change in the coming year
and they plan to make the following changes to their forecasts.
1 Reduce the selling price of the product by 10%.
2 Budget for a 20% increase in sales.
3 Budget for a 3% increase in direct labour.
4 Budget for a 10% decrease in fixed costs.
REQUIRED

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Calculate for product Wye:

parts.label: (i)
parts.text: the revised contribution per unit

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text: the revised break-even point in units

parts.label: (iii)
parts.text:
the revised margin of safety in units

Additional information
Another division of Hobbs Limited also manufactures one product, the Exe.
The following data is available for the year ending 30 June 2016.
Unit selling price $20
Unit variable costs $15
Budgeted fixed costs per annum $30000
Budgeted sales 8000 units
REQUIRED

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: Calculate the monthly break-even point in revenue.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text:
Prepare a break-even chart for product Exe for the year ending 30 June 2016. Clearly
indicate the areas of profit and loss.

parts.label: (e)
parts.text:
State three assumptions the accountant must make when preparing a break-even chart.

Additional information
The company uses marginal costing in order to calculate its break-even point for its ‘make or buy’
decisions.
REQUIRED

parts.label: (f)
parts.text:
State three further reasons why a business might use a marginal costing system.
